components.name: Contact Chip
components.description: Fixed-height linked contact image; kind prefix in ash, label in bone.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0; height: 36px; padding: 0 14px; border: 1px solid #4f4943; border-radius: 0; background: #0d1117; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 15px; text-decoration: none; white-space: pre; } .ds-chip-kind { color: #b8b1a9; font-weight: 400; } .ds-chip-label { color: #e6e5e4; font-weight: 800; } .ds-chip:hover, .ds-chip:focus-visible { border-color: #8c857b; outline: none; }

components.name: Section Header
components.description: Shell prompt as a section title, note right-aligned.
components.html: ~/src $ ls -lopen source, by commits
components.css: .ds-header { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; width: 776px; padding: 18px 32px 0; height: 52px; background: #0d1117; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 15px; } .ds-header-prompt { color: #e6e5e4; font-weight: 800; } .ds-header-note { color: #b8b1a9; font-weight: 400; }

components.name: Track Row
components.description: Project row: permission column, display title (amber when top-ranked), burn bar, count, description, metadata.
components.html:
drwxr-xr-xmosh@@@@@%%%%%######*****.........1,655

Encrypted desktop messenger on moss

May-Nov 2026 · dm, core, calls
components.css: .ds-track { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 108px 300px 282px 1fr; align-items: baseline; padding: 20px 32px; background: #0d1117; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 15px; color: #e6e5e4; } .ds-perm { color: #b8b1a9; } .ds-title { font-size: 32px; font-weight: 800; color: #e6e5e4; } .ds-title-top { color: #ffb43a; } .ds-bar { white-space: pre; color: #e6e5e4; } .ds-bar i { font-style: normal; color: #4f4943; } .ds-count { text-align: right; font-size: 20px; font-weight: 800; } .ds-desc, .ds-meta { grid-column: 2 / 5; margin: 4px 0 0; } .ds-meta { color: #b8b1a9; }

components.name: Burn Bar
components.description: Value as 30 cells burning from the densest glyph down, over a faint dotted track.
components.css: .ds-burn { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 15.7px; white-space: pre; background: #0d1117; padding: 8px; display: inline-block; filter: drop-shadow(0 0 2.5px rgb(230 229 228 / .22)); } .ds-burn .p { color: #e6e5e4; } .ds-burn .s { color: #b8b1a9; } .ds-burn .d { color: #8c857b; } .ds-burn .f { color: #4f4943; }

components.name: Ridge Chart
components.description: Glyph columns with a crest; hot columns burn amber at the top three rows.
components.css: .ds-ridge { margin: 0; padding: 8px; background: #0d1117; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 13px; line-height: 9px; color: #b8b1a9; } .ds-ridge b { color: #ffb43a; font-weight: 400; }

components.name: Cover Command
components.description: Cover call to action as a shell command with a blinking block cursor.
components.css: .ds-cmd { padding: 12px 32px; background: #0d1117; color: #e6e5e4; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 800; } .ds-cursor { display: inline-block; width: 9px; height: 16px; margin-left: 4px; vertical-align: -2px; background: #e6e5e4; animation: ds-blink 1.06s steps(1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-blink { 50% { opacity: 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-cursor { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Everything on the profile is one monospace character grid, and glyph density stands in for light. The avatar, the name, the per-project bars, the year of contributions and the hours of the day are all drawn from the same ten-step ramp (` .:-=+*#%@`). There are no solid fills, no charts in the dashboard sense, and no badges: a value is shown as how densely a run of characters burns. The terminal idiom (prompts like `~/src $ ls -l`, `drwxr-xr-x` permission columns, `cat` blocks, a blinking cursor) is the native grammar of the world, not decoration on top of it.

The palette is stone sampled from the avatar plus a single amber reserved for data peaks. The surface is GitHub's README column, which strips CSS and JS, so every visual is a generated SVG slice stacked full-width, each with its own subset of JetBrains Mono inlined. Neither theme paints a ground: the slices are transparent and ink sits directly on GitHub's own page colour (dark #0d1117, light white), because GitHub leaves a gap of page colour between stacked images and any painted slab would show a seam under every slice.

The same system is consumed outside this repo by the Spotify now-playing card (`D:\bprojects\me\worker\spotify-now-playing.js`), which closes the README: same stone and amber tiers, same ramp, a glyph-rendered album cover, JetBrains Mono inlined, and the same 840/420 wide/narrow widths and margins.
keyCharacteristics: One luminance ramp draws portrait, letterforms, bars and charts.
Stone in four reading tiers, amber only on data peaks.
One typeface, JetBrains Mono, at two weights (400, 800).
Transparent slices over GitHub's page colour in both themes.
Two layouts per slice: 840 wide, 420 narrow, swapped by `<picture>` media.
Terminal prompts as section headers, square 1px frames, no radius.

rules.name: The Peak-Only Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber marks a data peak and nothing else: the top-ranked project, the current year, the spike week, the night hours. If it is not a peak in real data, it is stone.

rules.name: The No-Ground Rule
rules.body: Slices are transparent in both themes. Ink sits on GitHub's own page colour; never paint a background slab, it seams between stacked images.

rules.name: The Density-Is-Tier Rule
rules.body: Glyph density maps to stone tier (ramp 0-2 faint, 3-4 dim, 5-6 secondary, 7-9 primary). Denser glyph, brighter tier.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono only, 400 and 800. Hierarchy comes from size, weight and stone tier, never a second family.

rules.name: The Line Budget Rule
rules.body: Text wraps greedily to the monospace character budget of its column (`floor(width / (size x 0.6))`), never by measured pixels.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-Dark-Only Rule
rules.body: Phosphor glow belongs to ink on a dark screen. Light theme is ink on paper and carries no glow.

dos: **Do** draw every quantity from the ramp ` .:-=+*#%@`, mapping density to stone tier.
**Do** keep amber for real data peaks: top project, current year, spike week, night hours.
**Do** render every slice in both layouts (840/32 and 420/20) and both themes.
**Do** leave slices transparent so ink sits on GitHub's page colour.
**Do** use shell idiom (prompts, permission columns, `cat`) for section structure.
**Do** inline only the glyphs a slice uses, as a JetBrains Mono woff2 subset.
donts: **Don't** use solid fills for bars, charts or letterforms; build them from glyph runs.
**Don't** paint a background in either theme.
**Don't** use amber for emphasis, links or decoration.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or corner radius.
**Don't** add badge or stats-card images; every number is a fetched value drawn in the grid.
**Don't** apply the phosphor glow in the light theme.
